title: Cross-Region Deployment Coordination and Saga Rollback Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the recommended process, verification steps, automation patterns, and escalation paths for coordinated cross-region service rollouts. It targets teams operating Redwood-managed multi-region services (hosted API, dedicated backends, and control-plane components) and emphasizes safety through orchestration sagas, gradual traffic steering, and explicit data migration windows.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce blast radius and mean time to recovery (MTTR) during cross-region deployments while preserving customer-facing SLAs.
- Scope: Application-level code rollouts, service configuration changes, global feature flags, DNS/edge changes, and schema-affecting DB migrations. Does NOT replace per-service runbooks for single-region rollouts.

Key principles:
1) Single source of truth for deployment state: use the platform deployment ledger (service-deployments.v1) for all long-running cross-region operations.
2) Break large changes into idempotent, reversible steps (saga pattern).
3) Prefer read-only traffic shadowing before write migrations.
4) Maintain region affinity and clear routing fallback policies.
5) Guard schema changes behind feature flags when possible.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Release owner: launches the saga, approves canary expansion. (Usually service PM/tech lead)
- Release engineer: runs the orchestration, monitors dashboards, initiates rollback if needed.
- Oncall SRE (regional): validates infra-level SLOs and participates in escalations.
- DBA / Data steward: approves migrations and verifies data consistency.
- Network ops: coordinates DNS/edge TTL changes and orchestrates global route modifications.

Pre-deploy checklist (required):
1) Deployment ticket opened in Jira with deployment plan, rollback criteria, and owners.
2) Canary configuration defined (percentage, regional targets, duration).
3) Backfill/shadow traffic plan for read paths if applicable.
4) DB migration plan with idempotency and backout scripts; dry-run in staging.
5) Dashboards and alerts pre-created (see Dashboard section).
6) DNS/edge TTL planned (default <= 60s for quick rollbacks) and approved by Network ops.
7) Runbook link attached to the release ticket and shared with oncall.

Saga coordinate pattern (high-level steps):
1) Prestage: deploy new artifacts to all regions but do not switch traffic. Verify health checks and node-level metrics for 15–30m.
2) Canary region: enable new version in a single region at 1–5% traffic. Monitor for business and infra metrics.
3) Progressive ramp: increase traffic in the canary region in discrete steps (1→5→25→50) with stabilization windows.
4) Cross-region propagation: once canary is healthy for 2 consecutive stabilization windows, enable the new version in additional regions following regional order (typically least-latency or low-traffic first).
5) Global cutover: when all regions are healthy and data migrations completed, flip global route priorities or update DNS weights.
6) Final verification: run end-to-end smoke tests and run selected production prompts through canary verification harness.
7) Close saga: mark deployment successful in ledger and document any postmortem items.

Rollback decision criteria (examples):
- Business errors: user-visible error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes or > 0.2% for 15 minutes.
- Latency regressions: 95th percentile latency increased > 40% vs baseline for 10 minutes.
- Infrastructure failures: node crash rate > 3% in newly deployed cluster or repeated OOMs.
- Data anomalies: sequence gaps, constraint violations, or replication lag > 120s during write migration.

Rollback steps (fast path):
1) Immediately set the service-level traffic weight for the new version to 0% via the platform router API. Example:
   curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"service":"orders","region":"us-west-2","weight":0}' https://platform-router.internal/api/v1/weights
2) Revert DNS weights if DNS-based steering was used (update TTL to 30s and reapply previous weights).
3) Reopen previous canary nodes to accept write traffic and confirm health.
4) Notify stakeholders in #releases and update the release ticket with timeline and reason.
5) If rollback affects schema, run db backout scripts and validate.

Rollback steps (data-migration-safe path):
- If changes are read-only or behind feature flags, simply disable the flag and let system degrade gracefully. Then perform a targeted data reconciliation.

Dashboards and alerts (templates):
- Dashboard: Cross-Region Rollout — per-region panels for:
  | Metric | Panel | Threshold |
  |-------|-------|-----------|
  | Requests/sec | Line (per-region) | - |
  | HTTP 5xx rate | Stacked area | alert if > 0.5% sustained |
  | p95 latency | Heatmap | alert if > 40% over baseline |
  | Node restarts | Bar | alert if > 3% of nodes restarted in 10m |
  | DB replication lag | Line | alert if > 120s |
- Alerting rules (examples):
  1) cross_region_high_5xx: triggers when 5xx_rate > 0.5% for 5m. Pager duty: backend-oncall. Severity: P1.
  2) cross_region_latency_regression: p95 > baseline*1.4 for 10m. Pager duty: perf-oncall. Severity: P2.
  3) db_migration_lagging: replication_lag > 120s for 2m. Pager duty: data-oncall. Severity: P1.

Example alert configuration (YAML):
---
alert: cross_region_high_5xx
expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",job=~"orders.*"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=~"orders.*"}[5m])) > 0.005
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: p1
  team: backend
annotations:
  summary: "Cross-region 5xx spike for {{ $labels.job }}"
---

DNS and edge considerations:
- Keep DNS TTL <= 60s for cross-region flips during a rollout window.
- Use weighted routing with fallback to the nearest healthy region.
- Avoid simultaneous global CDN config changes unless coordinated with Network ops and CDN provider.

Database migration guidance:
- Favor online, backward-compatible changes (add columns with default NULL, create new tables).
- For destructive migrations, create a two-step plan: (A) introduce new schema elements and ensure code can write/read both old and new; (B) schedule a maintenance window to remove old artifacts.
- Run data migration in small batches with progress checkpoints logged to the deployment ledger.

Pre- and post-deploy verification commands (examples):
- Smoke test (run from CI runner in target region):
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMOKE_TOKEN" https://orders.us-west-2.api.redwood/v1/health | jq .status
- Check replication lag (Postgres example):
  SELECT now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() AS replication_lag;
- Verify region-specific routing:
  dig +short orders.api.redwood | xargs -I{} curl -sS -H "Host: orders.api.redwood" http://{} /health

Communication and windows:
- Rollout windows should be defined in the ticket (start, expected duration, blackout hours). Prefer low-traffic windows for global cutovers.
- Notify customer success and product in advance for any changes that may impact SLAs.
- Use #releases (public) for high-level updates and #releases-private for sensitive rollouts.

Post-deploy: runbook closure items:
1) Execute a 24–72 hour watch with daily checks for regression.
2) Create a short retrospective if any rollback or unexpected incidents occurred. Document causes, timeline, and remediation.
3) Update runbook and automation scripts with lessons learned.

Retrospective triggers (automatic):
- Any P1/P0 incident during the rollout.
- Rollback initiated.
- Post-deploy error budget burn > 40% in 24h.

Automation and tooling recommendations:
- Use the orchestration service (deploy-orchestrator) which supports saga steps, retries, and compensating actions.
- Store deployment intent and state in the deployment ledger. Do not rely solely on CI logs.
- Provide a one-click rollback shortcut in the deployment UI that executes the fast-path rollback.

Appendix A — Quick checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Jira ticket with owners and rollback criteria
- [ ] Dashboards and alerts created
- [ ] DNS TTL & edge plan approved
- [ ] DB migration dry-run complete
- [ ] Canary defined and automation configured
- [ ] Runbook link attached and oncall notified

Appendix B — Example saga step JSON (for deploy-orchestrator):
{
  "saga_id": "deploy-2025-09-orders-v1.4.0",
  "steps": ["prestage","canary-us-west-2","monitor-15m","ramp-to-50","propagate-eu-west-1","global-cutover"]
}
